artifact_snapshot_digest.ambiguity_rule: Two entries sharing a content_sha256, or any entry whose content_sha256 does not resolve to exactly one active operational artifact, is a corrupt inventory and fails closed. catalog.artifacts declares UNIQUE (content_sha256), so a duplicate can only come from a hand-edited or truncated manifest.
artifact_snapshot_digest.count_rule: artifact_count and artifact_total_bytes are the row count and the SUM(size_bytes) of exactly the rows the predicate selects - no other row contributes to either.
artifact_snapshot_digest.note: Domain separation makes an artifact-snapshot digest unusable as a recovery-manifest digest even if the two documents ever serialize identically.

artifact_snapshot_predicate.note: The three artifacts a recovery set is made of carry backup_scope = 'recovery', so they can never appear in the operational snapshot they describe. The snapshot is therefore a fixed point: registering a recovery set does not change the inventory that recovery set hashes.
artifact_snapshot_predicate.sql: SELECT content_sha256, size_bytes, artifact_kind FROM catalog.artifacts WHERE lifecycle_state = 'active' AND backup_scope = 'operational' ORDER BY content_sha256, size_bytes, artifact_kind

cutover_mapping.executed_in: a later stage, not D1.1 and not D2

postgresql_dependency_analysis.consequence: Every SECURITY DEFINER function, every SET search_path and every textual object reference must be re-created or re-verified as part of the cutover transaction, not assumed correct. This is why step 5 exists and why a rename alone is not a cutover.
renames_that_do_NOT_follow_automatically: A function body is stored as TEXT and is re-parsed at execution time: a schema-qualified reference inside a SECURITY DEFINER body keeps naming the OLD schema after a rename and will silently resolve to the retired V1 object.
SET search_path attached to a function, a role or the database names schemas as strings and does not follow a rename.
regclass and regprocedure values stored as TEXT rather than as the regclass type.
Any schema name embedded in application SQL or configuration.
renames_that_follow_automatically: Foreign keys, indexes, sequences, primary keys and check constraints track their table by OID, so a schema rename does not break them.
Views and column defaults parsed into stored parse trees track referenced objects by OID as well.

preconditions: Application writes stopped and active transactions drained.
A complete recovery set verified: the database backup AND its artifact snapshot.
revalidation_targets: foreign keys resolve to the renamed schemas
function bodies and their SET search_path clauses
trigger definitions and the functions they call
database, role and session search_path configuration
regclass / regprocedure literals stored in catalogs or column defaults
SQL text embedded in views, defaults, check constraints and function bodies
repository-side schema resolution in the application

steps.detail: database backup plus artifact snapshot, both verified

In the SAME transaction as the renames, CREATE OR REPLACE every one of the 34 DB-V2 functions with its body qualified against the CANONICAL schema names, then re-verify every trigger still names its function and every grant in the ACL matrix still resolves.
commit only if every revalidation target passes

database_api.note: The executable half of the contract: every function, trigger, state transition and grant migration 0009 must create. Frozen in DB-V2 D1.4.

deployment_mapping.note: Alembic's own revision marker. One row, one table, shared by V1 and the shadow deployment; it is never duplicated into a dbv2_* schema.

forbidden_migration_shortcuts: alembic stamp to fake a revision the database never executed
rewriting migrations 0001-0008, whose byte hashes are cited in accepted evidence
manual UPDATE or INSERT against public.alembic_version
destructive in-place conversion of a V1 table
undocumented table-name suffixes such as _v2 or _new to dodge a collision

alembic_lineage.resolution: A controlled operational preparation that walks the real lineage 0005 -> 0006 -> 0007 -> 0008 -> 0009, verifying zero L2-F business rows after each intermediate revision.
alembic_lineage.summary: A future 0009 with down_revision=0008 cannot be applied to an operational database at 0005: Alembic must execute 0006, 0007 and 0008 first. D1 implied 0006-0008 would stay unapplied after DB-V2 deployment, which is not reachable.

physical_collision.resolution: A frozen temporary physical schema namespace (dbv2_*). The logical contract is unchanged; only the deployment-time schema differs.
physical_collision.summary: D1 described V2 shadow tables coexisting with untouched V1 tables, but the logical target reuses schema-qualified names that V1 already occupies. Creating them side by side in one database is impossible.

qualification_period_semantics.canonical_schemas_mean: V2. During qualification, catalog/profiling/experiments/evaluation/models/runtime/audit resolve to the migrated V2 objects.
qualification_period_semantics.dbv2_names_after_forward_cutover: absent. The dbv2_* schemas were renamed to canonical, so those names no longer exist.
qualification_period_semantics.dbv2_names_after_rollback: present again, recreated by renaming the canonical V2 schemas back to dbv2_*.
qualification_period_semantics.deletions_of_v2: none. No V2 object is deleted during the qualification period.
qualification_period_semantics.v1_retired_holds: the rollback source - the untouched V1 objects under v1_retired_* names
qualification_period_semantics.writes_to_retired_v1: none. No retired V1 object is written during qualification.

r1_manifest_conditional_fields.rule: Present and non-null exactly when the recovery set is 'complete'. A 'database_only' manifest carries these three as null, and the registered row carries them as NULL.

ordering_invariants: R2 strictly follows revision 0009 and strictly precedes any data transformation.
No recovery row is ever written to a V1 relation.
No transformation or cutover may begin while completeness != 'complete'.
Downgrading 0009 never deletes an R1 recovery file.

phases.canonical_bytes_rule: The manifest is serialized with the repository's canonical JSON encoder (sorted keys, tight separators, UTF-8, newline-terminated). recovery_manifest_sha256 = sha256(canonical_json_bytes(the complete R1 manifest)). The digest is over the WHOLE manifest, so no field can be altered without changing it.
phases.completeness_rule: A database dump WITHOUT the matching artifact snapshot is incomplete and may not be used to authorize a migration.

coordinated_capture.failure_rule: If ANY step fails, the R1 set is incomplete: migration 0009 is not authorized, no transformation begins, and the partial recovery files are left in place for inspection rather than deleted.

steps.step: Stop application writes and artifact publication. Every writing service is drained or stopped; no new artifact bytes are published.
Drain active write transactions. Wait until no non-read-only backend holds an open transaction against the database; record quiesce_started_at once the drain completes.
Capture the database backup and the WAL position inside the quiesced window (pg_dump -Fc plus pg_current_wal_lsn()).
Enumerate and verify the operational artifact snapshot using the EXACT predicate lifecycle_state = 'active' AND backup_scope = 'operational', digesting every payload.
Publish the database backup, the snapshot manifest and the recovery manifest beneath MINOS_DB_RECOVERY_ROOT using the atomic publication protocol.
Re-read every published file and verify its bytes against its recorded digest.
Record quiesce_ended_at and resume writes ONLY after the complete R1 set is durable on disk.

coordinated_capture.why: An independently timed pg_dump and filesystem scan do NOT form one recovery point: artifacts published between the two would appear in the snapshot but not the dump, or the reverse, and the recovery set would describe a state the system was never in. The quiesce is what makes the database backup and the artifact snapshot one consistent operational state, and quiesce_started_at/quiesce_ended_at are recorded so that claim is auditable rather than asserted.
coordinated_capture.withdrawn_claim: that an independently timed pg_dump and filesystem scan together form one recovery point

phases.name: external recovery manifest
phases.rationale: dbv2_catalog.backup_sets does not exist yet, and V1 has no catalog.backup_sets at all. The manifest is a FILE on durable storage outside the repository and outside the database, not a database row, and must not be described as one.
phases.snapshot_predicate: SELECT content_sha256, size_bytes, artifact_kind FROM catalog.artifacts WHERE lifecycle_state = 'active' AND backup_scope = 'operational' ORDER BY content_sha256, size_bytes, artifact_kind
phases.storage: external file beneath MINOS_DB_RECOVERY_ROOT, outside PostgreSQL
verification: the database backup is restorable into a scratch cluster
every artifact payload selected by the snapshot predicate digests to its recorded content_sha256
artifact_count and artifact_total_bytes match the enumerated snapshot exactly
no artifact with backup_scope = 'recovery' appears in the snapshot
every published recovery file re-reads to its recorded digest

phases.downgrade_rule: Downgrading 0009 removes the dbv2_catalog.backup_sets rows but MUST NOT delete any R1 recovery file. The files under MINOS_DB_RECOVERY_ROOT are the authoritative pre-migration record and outlive every database object.
phases.forbidden_target_reason: V1 has no catalog.backup_sets relation; writing there is impossible, and the canonical name belongs to V2 only after cutover.
phases.idempotency: A re-run with the same recovery_set_id and the same immutable data is a no-op. The same recovery_set_id or backup_key with ANY differing immutable value fails closed; it never overwrites.
phases.name: register the R1 manifest in the shadow schema
registration_steps: Read the R1 manifest bytes from the recovery root.
Strictly parse them with duplicate-key rejection.
Recompute recovery_manifest_sha256 over the canonical bytes and require it to equal the published name and the recorded value.

For a complete set, recompute artifact_snapshot_sha256 over the snapshot manifest's canonical bytes with its domain prefix, and require the entry count and total size to equal artifact_count and artifact_total_bytes.

Publish/register the recovery artifacts with get-or-verify behaviour, each with backup_scope = 'recovery': the recovery manifest and the database backup always, the artifact-snapshot manifest only for a complete set.
Insert dbv2_catalog.backup_sets using their exact artifact ids, digests and media types.
catalog.enforce_backup_set_shape() runs as a CONSTRAINT trigger in the same transaction and performs the full cross-table verification; a failure aborts the insert.
Re-read the inserted row AND the referenced catalog.artifacts rows.
Require exact equality with the R1 manifest, field for field.
phases.retention_of_external_manifest: The R1 file is kept for the life of the backup set it describes, beneath MINOS_DB_RECOVERY_ROOT. Downgrading 0009 destroys the database row but not the file, which is exactly why the file is the authoritative pre-migration record.
rules: Insert exactly the R1 manifest's fields; invent nothing.
Re-read the inserted row and require field-for-field equality with the verified R1 manifest.
Require completeness = 'complete' before any transformation or cutover.
The R1 files are retained unchanged as recovery evidence after registration.
phases.shape_rule: A 'complete' insert registers three artifacts; a 'database_only' insert registers two and carries the snapshot triple and both counts as NULL. The two shapes are enforced all-or-none by ck_backup_sets_shape and cross-table by catalog.enforce_backup_set_shape().

recovery_set_protocol.summary: A recovery set must exist BEFORE any migration, but the table that records it (dbv2_catalog.backup_sets) is created BY that migration. D1 required a catalog.backup_sets row at step 1, which is unexecutable: no such relation exists in V1 and the V2 one does not exist yet. The protocol is therefore two-phase.

recovery_storage_contract.default_note: There is NO default and no repository-relative fallback. If the variable is unset, recovery publication fails closed. A default would silently select the source checkout, which is exactly the defect this replaces.

must_differ_from: the active artifact payload root (MINOS_L2F_RESULT_ARTIFACT_ROOT and the L2-D corpus)
durability_separation.rule: The recovery root must be on durable storage SEPARATE from all three of the following, so that losing any one of them does not lose the recovery evidence.
durability_separation.verification: compare the resolved device and the resolved path prefix of each; a shared device or a containment relationship fails closed

git_rules.gitignore_note: No .gitignore entry is added, because no repository-relative path is reachable at all. An entry would imply such a path exists.

recovery_storage_contract.immutability: A published recovery file is never rewritten. A second publication of the same digest is a verified no-op; a different payload under the same digest is impossible by construction and a same-name different-digest collision fails closed on the no-clobber link.
publication_protocol: write to a mkstemp temporary file inside the destination directory
fchmod to 0o640 and verify the resulting credentials
hard-link into place with no-clobber semantics (link(2), never rename over)
re-open and verify the published bytes digest to the expected sha256
remove only inodes this call proved it created
root_requirements: must already exist; the application never creates it
must never be silently repaired, chmod-ed or chown-ed by the application
must not be a symlink, and no component of it may be a symlink
must be a directory owned by the publishing user

supersedes.why_wrong: A source-repository path. Writing runtime recovery evidence there dirties the Git checkout and loses the evidence together with the application host - the two failures a recovery set exists to survive.

retirement.authorized_in: a later stage, only after qualification passes; never in D1.2 or D2
retirement.namespace_rule: Retirement may affect ONLY the v1_retired_* namespace. No canonical schema or table is ever a retirement target, because after cutover the canonical names are the live V2 system.
per_object_checks_before_removal: no remaining foreign key, view, function or trigger depends on the object
row count matches the value recorded at cutover, or is zero where zero was expected
every identity the object carried is provably present in its V2 successor
the object has not been written since cutover
retirement.schema_drop_rule: Prefer dropping a complete v1_retired_* schema, and only after every object it contains has individually passed its retirement check.

revision_path.development_lifecycle_note: Scratch PostgreSQL only: up, down, up again, proving 0009 is reversible without touching any operational store.
intermediate_revision_invariants: 0006, 0007 and 0008 remain byte-identical and are never rewritten.
They are unapplied operationally TODAY, and will execute as structural predecessors during the future controlled preparation.
After each intermediate revision, every L2-F table must hold zero business rows.
No artifact publication, job enqueue or execution may occur during the intermediate revisions.
No application path runs Alembic automatically; migration is an explicit operator action.

rollback_boundaries.db_state: operational database at 0005..0008; no DB-V2 object exists
rollback_boundaries.name: before 0009
procedure: Nothing DB-V2 needs undoing: no dbv2_* schema, table, function or grant exists.
If recovery is required for an unrelated reason, restore from the verified R1 recovery set (database backup AND artifact snapshot).

rollback_boundaries.db_state: dbv2_* shadow schema exists; canonical schemas are still V1
rollback_boundaries.drops_v2_note: Dropping the shadow schema is correct HERE and only here: the canonical names still belong to V1, so nothing live is lost.
rollback_boundaries.name: after 0009, before cutover
procedure: The downgrade removes ONLY dbv2_* objects.
It must not alter, rename, delete or write any V1 object.
public.alembic_version changes only through Alembic's own bookkeeping.

rollback_boundaries.db_state: canonical schemas are V2; v1_retired_* holds the rollback source
rollback_boundaries.drops_v2_note: The returned dbv2_* schema is NOT dropped inside the rollback transaction. It is the evidence of what was rolled back. Retiring V2 is a separately authorized cleanup, only after recovery is proven.
rollback_boundaries.name: after cutover, during qualification
procedure: Quiesce writes and drain active transactions.
Rename each canonical V2 schema back to its dbv2_* name.
Rename each v1_retired_* schema back to its canonical name.
Re-create or revalidate functions, SET search_path clauses, textual regclass references, grants and application schema resolution.
Commit only if every rollback validation passes.
rollback_boundaries.touches_v1_note: V1 is renamed back to canonical - it is never altered, deleted or written.

rollback_mapping.note: The rollback is the exact inverse permutation of the cutover: applying cutover then rollback returns every schema to its starting name.
rollback_mapping.precondition: writes quiesced, exactly as for the forward cutover

steps.detail: In the SAME transaction as the renames, CREATE OR REPLACE every one of the 34 DB-V2 functions with its body qualified against the dbv2_* shadow schema names, then re-verify every trigger still names its function and every grant in the ACL matrix still resolves.

rollback_mapping.trigger: any revalidation target fails, or a qualification defect is found while the shadow schema is serving

schema_mapping.note: dbv2_* are DEPLOYMENT names, not the final application contract. After cutover every schema carries its canonical name again and application code never references a dbv2_* identifier.

trigger_deployment.note: Triggers are attached to the dbv2_* shadow tables and track them by OID, so the schema rename does not detach them. Their FUNCTION reference is by OID as well; what does NOT follow the rename is the schema-qualified text INSIDE each function body, which is why every function is re-created in the cutover transaction.

v1_objects_d2_must_preserve.rule: D2 and D3 create only dbv2_* objects. They never rename, alter, delete or write any V1 object, and they never write to public.alembic_version except through Alembic's own revision bookkeeping.

withdrawn_statements.replaced_by: rollback boundary B3 - the inverse schema rename.
withdrawn_statements.statement: post-cutover rollback is performed by pointing repositories at V1 and dropping the shadow tables
withdrawn_statements.why_wrong: After cutover the shadow tables ARE the live system under canonical names. Dropping them would delete the migrated database, and 'V1 repositories' no longer resolve to V1 because canonical names belong to V2.

withdrawn_statements.statement: record a catalog.backup_sets row as migration step 1
withdrawn_statements.why_wrong: V1 has no catalog.backup_sets relation and the V2 one is created by the migration that step 1 precedes.

withdrawn_statements.replaced_by: retirement targets in the v1_retired_* namespace only.
withdrawn_statements.statement: final retirement drops canonical objects such as catalog.datasets and profiling.profiles
withdrawn_statements.why_wrong: After cutover those canonical names are LIVE V2 tables. catalog.datasets is simultaneously a declared logical V2 table, so the instruction would drop the migrated system.

withdrawn_statements.replaced_by: an externally provisioned MINOS_DB_RECOVERY_ROOT with no default and no repository-relative fallback.
withdrawn_statements.statement: the R1 recovery manifest lives at reports/database/recovery/R1_RECOVERY_MANIFEST.json
withdrawn_statements.why_wrong: That is a source-repository path. Runtime recovery evidence written there dirties the Git checkout and is lost together with the application host.

withdrawn_statements.replaced_by: boundary-aware wording: pre-cutover downgrade 0009->0008; post-cutover transactional inverse schema rename.
withdrawn_statements.statement: the strategy table's rollback entry 'Point the application back; drop the shadow.'
withdrawn_statements.why_wrong: It contradicts the required post-cutover inverse schema rename and would delete the migrated system.

withdrawn_statements.replaced_by: the coordinated R1 quiesce protocol in recovery_set_protocol.phases[R1]
withdrawn_statements.statement: that an independently timed pg_dump and filesystem artifact scan together form one recovery point
withdrawn_statements.why_wrong: Artifacts published between the two would appear in one half and not the other, so the recovery set would describe a state the system was never in.

withdrawn_statements.replaced_by: the exact predicate lifecycle_state = 'active' AND backup_scope = 'operational'
withdrawn_statements.statement: that the R1 artifact snapshot covers every active artifact
withdrawn_statements.why_wrong: R2 makes three more artifacts active and verified, so re-running an unqualified 'all active artifacts' predicate after R2 yields a different digest than the one R1 recorded. The snapshot would never be reproducible.
